rationale: Go's named extraction is exact, so its floor is exact: all 76 function_declaration and 132 method_declaration nodes here become Callables, and Go has no nested named function form for a walker to miss. A named_funcs floor below 1.0 would let a real regression through silently. The 0.4% call shortfall is 5 of 1265 nodes and every one of them is a callee with no name to record: 4 are `c.UsageFunc()(c)` — calling the function a call returned, where the inner call already emits `UsageFunc` — and 1 is an immediately-invoked `func() { ... }()`. Their `function` field holds a call_expression or a func_literal rather than an identifier or a selector, so the only way to emit an edge would be to synthesize a name, which ADR-0031 rejects. Across the whole cobra checkout the same shapes are the entire remainder: 22 of 4430 (0.5%) — 17 IIFEs, 4 call-of-call, and 1 `(*customMultiString)(nil)` parenthesized type conversion that is not a call at all. What did move is the closure body: 177 of these 1265 call nodes sit inside a func_literal and are now attributed to the enclosing named function per ADR-0031, where before ATL-096 all of them vanished (cobra-wide: 0.888 -> 0.995). Note the ratio measures walker reach, not edge usefulness — Go spells type conversions and builtins as call_expression, so 166 `len`/`append`/`make` calls and 4 `string`/`int64` conversions count as covered here and resolve to nothing downstream. Files chosen for closure density rather than size: this fixture runs 14.0% of calls inside a literal against the repo's 10.0%, so a walker that stops at func_literal again fails harder here than on the source repo. No uid collides; Go has no construct that can produce two same-named definitions in one package scope.
